title: Knowledge check: Static and Dynamic Content Delivery

questions.prompt: In Static and Dynamic Content Delivery, which statement best describes Choosing static files versus generated responses?
options: Move all backend decisions into the browser and trust the submitted values.
Return the same success response for every request regardless of outcome.
Choose static delivery, server rendering or a separate frontend according to the product need. Escape untrusted template output and do not expose private files through public asset paths.
Measure representative traffic first, then optimize the measured bottleneck. Cache only data with an explicit freshness/invalidation policy and bound results and concurrent work.
questions.answer_key: Choose static delivery, server rendering or a separate frontend according to the product need. Escape untrusted template output and do not expose private files through public asset paths.
questions.explanation: Choose static delivery, server rendering or a separate frontend according to the product need. Escape untrusted template output and do not expose private files through public asset paths.

questions.prompt: Which design rule is most appropriate when applying Static and Dynamic Content Delivery?
options: Assume that adding CORS makes private routes authenticated.

Static files, server-rendered views, and separate frontends serve different needs. Keep private uploads away from public static directories, escape template output, and treat CORS and auth as separate concerns.
Trust request fields and skip authorization to keep handlers small.
Suppress all errors without recording safe diagnostic information.
questions.answer_key: Static files, server-rendered views, and separate frontends serve different needs. Keep private uploads away from public static directories, escape template output, and treat CORS and auth as separate concerns.
questions.explanation: Static files, server-rendered views, and separate frontends serve different needs. Keep private uploads away from public static directories, escape template output, and treat CORS and auth as separate concerns.

questions.prompt: A change related to Static and Dynamic Content Delivery appears to work for one normal request. What is the strongest next verification step?
options: Use repeatable tests for a successful request and at least one invalid/boundary or dependency-failure case.
Test only one successful request manually and record no expected output.
Use production data to avoid building a small reproducible fixture.
Treat the page’s displayed reference output as proof that Node.js executed the code.
questions.answer_key: Use repeatable tests for a successful request and at least one invalid/boundary or dependency-failure case.
questions.explanation: Use repeatable tests for a successful request and at least one invalid/boundary or dependency-failure case.
